subject: Subprocessor handling of PII, KMS custody & redaction/pseudonymization approach
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novamed.ai
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on subprocessors that may process PII + pseudonymization approach

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the DPA draft — our legal team sent back a few targeted questions on subprocessors and how Redwood handles PII in practice. To help us close the security review, could you confirm the following?

1) Which named subprocessors (by role) will have the ability to access unredacted PII during normal operations (not just for incident response)? Specifically: logging/telemetry ingestion, model training/embedding pipelines, inference runtime.

2) For each of those subprocessors, who holds the KMS keys (Redwood, customer-managed KMS, or third-party key custodian)? If Redwood holds keys, what safeguards and split-key protections do you maintain?

3) Do you perform pseudonymization/redaction at ingestion or do you rely on runtime masking? We need a brief description of the algorithmic approach and whether it is reversible by any subprocessor.

4) Can you share a simple dataflow diagram that shows where PII is stored, where it is tokenized/pseudonymized, and the trust boundary between Redwood, dedicated providers, and any third parties?

If possible, wed appreciate sample artifacts (a one-page matrix of subprocessors + key custody, and a minimal pseudonymization flow diagram) by EOD tomorrow — our security committee meets on Wednesday.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if thats easier.

Best,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Security, Novamed
elena.ruiz@novamed.ai

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.ai>
Cc: priya.natarajan@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 11:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on subprocessors that may process PII + pseudonymization approach

Elena — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; attaching a concise matrix and a flow diagram to start. We'll follow up with formal evidence artifacts for the DPA annex.

1) Subprocessors with potential access to unredacted PII (normal ops):
- Ingestion & telemetry pipeline: Redwood-managed telemetry ingestion service (we operate the service; logs that contain PII are encrypted and access-limited).
- Inference runtime: model serving nodes (we run on dedicated pools or customer-dedicated deployments; for Hosted customers, runtime may touch customer-provided prompt content).
- Data labeling/training (only for customers who opt into model improvement programs) — this is an opt-in pipeline and data is pseudonymized before labeling.

2) KMS custody:
- Hosted (default): Redwood-managed KMS held by Redwood with HSM-backed keys. We use envelope encryption and rotate per-customer keys; split-key protections and role-based access control limit operator access.
- Dedicated/Private: customer-managed KMS or HSM is supported; in those cases Redwood never has plaintext key material.
(See attached subprocessor_matrix_v2.xlsx — column C notes key custody per role.)

3) Pseudonymization/redaction:
- By default we recommend pseudonymization at ingestion for structured identifiers (SSNs, emails, phone numbers) using deterministic tokenization that is reversible only with an HSM-held wrapping key. For free-text prompts we provide optional runtime redaction/masking hooks; customers can enable on-prem proxies to perform client-side redaction before ingestion.
- For customers who enable Redwoods labeling pipeline, data is pseudonymized using a one-way hash + salt before leaving the production cluster.
(See pseudonymization_flow.pdf for the flow and reversible vs non-reversible paths.)

4) Dataflow diagram: attached (pseudonymization_flow.pdf) and also a Drive doc with more context: https://drive.google.com/doc/d/1A2b3Csubproc-plan

Next steps:
- Priya, can you confirm the split-key/hsm attestation language we can share as evidence?
- Marissa, can you draft a short DPA annex paragraph clarifying Hosted vs Dedicated key custody and the opt-in labeling behavior?

Elena — happy to schedule a 30-minute walkthrough. Are you available Tuesday 10–11am PT?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), pseudonymization_flow.pdf (diagram)

Also flagging that Novamed asked about runtime masking for free-text prompts. Priya, if we have a short tech note on optional client-side proxies or on-prem agents that do pre-ingestion redaction, drop it into the Drive link.

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Subprocessor handling of PII, KMS custody & redaction/pseudonymization approach

On Mon, Aug 11, 2025 at 11:09 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Elena — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; attaching a concise matrix and a flow diagram to start. We'll follow up with formal evidence artifacts for the DPA annex.

Hi all — quick update and a few clarifications for Novamed:

- HSM/KMS attestation: Redwood uses HSMs certified to FIPS 140-2 Level 3 (HSM vendor: Thales) for our Redwood-managed KMS. Key wrapping and envelope encryption are standard; we never store customer plaintext keys. Operational access to unwrap keys requires multi-party approval workflows and recorded RBAC audit logs (we can provide a redacted log sample).

- Split-key protections: we perform key-splitting for high-sensitivity workstreams (SOC-level escalations) and require multi-admin approval for key reconstruction. This is in our internal attestation; we will create a one-paragraph attestation for Novamed (expect in next email).

- Pseudonymization details: deterministic tokenization for structured identifiers (reversible using HSM-wrapped keys only). For free-text we provide two options: 1) runtime client-side redaction (recommended for highest assurance: pre-ingestion), or 2) Redwood runtime masking that replaces detected identifiers with tokens; runtime masking keys are HSM-protected and access-limited. The labeling pipeline receives only pseudonymized artifacts unless a customer explicitly opts to de-pseudonymize under a narrow, audited workflow.

- Attachments: Ive uploaded a short attestation draft and the redaction sample to the Drive doc.

Elena — if youd like, I can join the Tue/Wed walkthrough to run through attestation details.

Priya Natarajan
Senior Manager, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
